transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sarah Lee (Nimbus Head of ML), Tom Watkins (Nimbus CTO), Priya Singh (Nimbus Data Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Sarah: Hi thanks, Sarah here. We're excited to dig in, short intro, we're building a clinical search product for clinicians to find relevant patient notes and guidelines.
[00:20] Tom: Tom, CTO, high-level goals are latency under 150ms p50 for interactive search and high recall for rare terms.
[00:28] Priya: Priya, I own the search infra and embeddings pipeline.
[00:33] Diego: Great, we'll keep this focused on embeddings and reranking — vector DB choices, throughput, dimensionality, and hybrid search patterns. quick question: do you currently use any vector DB?
[00:45] Priya: We're prototyping with FAISS locally, and we also tested Pinecone for a short POC. FAISS is fast but ops-heavy. Pinecone simplified ops but cost scaled and some distance metric differences caused variance.
[01:05] Maya: Helpful. what's your current embedding model and dimensionality?
[01:10] Priya: We're on a 1536-d dense embedding from a third-party model (name gets fuzzy in doc), but we also tried 768-d smaller models. 1536 gives better recall on long clinical notes but costs more.
[01:24] Sarah: Also regulatory note, data residency for EU patients matters, and audit logs/retention are required.
[01:31] Diego: Makes sense. on the Redwood side, we support Hosted API for quick starts, Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools if you want predictable throughput, and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads. For compliance, we have KMS integrations and audit logging.
[01:48] Tom: For us the decision is about predictable latency and data isolation. If we move to Dedicated or Private we need SLA and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
[01:59] Maya: We can do CMK via KMS/HSM and provide audit logs. I'll attach the SOC2 + ISO packet.
[02:06] Priya: On search architecture, we're considering a hybrid approach: BM25 for initial recall followed by ANN-based rerank. want to understand how Redwood can fit in that pipeline.
[02:18] Diego: That's a common pattern. A typical architecture we see: lightweight lexical filter -> ANN nearest neighbors via a vector DB (FAISS/HNSW) -> cross-encoder/reranker for final ranking. Redwood can provide embeddings at scale and host the rerank model for low-latency inference, or you can keep embeddings in your vector DB and call our hosted reranker.
[02:39] Sarah: For the reranker, latency budget is tight. We can't do cross-encoder on 100 candidates at query time, it's too slow. We're thinking 20-50 candidates, but we'd like to understand throughput tradeoffs.
[02:50] Diego: Yep, that's typical. we recommend retrieval of 100 candidates from ANN, then a learned lightweight reranker (e.g., a distilled cross-encoder or bi-encoder with interaction layers) to rerank top 20. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization for the reranker to hit latency SLOs.
[03:08] Tom: Quantization — curious if Redwood supports int8 or mixed precision for the rerank models?
[03:14] Diego: We support quantized runtimes and CPU fallbacks; Dedicated pools allow optimized kernels and int8 paths. Quantization can reduce memory by 2-4x and speed up inference, but you need to validate regression on held-out prompts.
[03:28] Priya: about dimensionality: is there a recommended sweet spot? 1536 works but it's heavy. 768 was close on some metrics. any rules of thumb?
[03:36] Diego: It depends — higher dims generally help for subtle semantic differences, especially with clinical jargon. But you can often get similar downstream rerank performance with 768 if your reranker is strong. We usually recommend benchmarking 512/768/1536 on a small eval set and looking at recall@k and rerank NDCG. Redwood can run those benchmarks on Dedicated to give you latency + cost profiles.
[03:59] Sarah: Can Redwood's embeddings be customized or fine-tuned to our corpus?
[04:04] Maya: Yes, we can host tuned models and support fine-tuning or instruction tuning pipelines; there are tradeoffs on maintenance. For most teams, adapting the reranker is cheaper than fine-tuning a large embedding model.
[04:17] Tom: Integration with our current vector DB — we use FAISS for on-prem and Pinecone for cloud experiments. How does Redwood connect?
[04:26] Diego: Two patterns: 1) You manage embeddings in your vector DB; call Redwood for rerank/LLM tasks. 2) Use Redwood-hosted embeddings and store vectors in your DB via export APIs. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can run co-located inference nodes to minimize egress and network latency. For FAISS we typically recommend HNSW indexes for recall/latency balance.
[04:47] Priya: We also have a legal requirement to purge patient data after X days. How does Redwood handle deletion and retention?
[04:54] Maya: We have deletion APIs, retention policies, and can configure shorter retention for Dedicated/Private. We'll include retention and purge details in the security packet.
[05:04] Sarah: A perf question: our peak QPS for search is around 80 qps with bursts to 250 qps during morning rounds. Latency target p95 under 300ms, p50 under 150ms. what's realistic?
[05:20] Diego: For embeddings-only calls, Hosted can handle it if you're okay with multi-tenant variability. For predictable 80–250 qps with tight p95, Dedicated is the right fit. With batching and smart KV/prefix caching, we've seen p50 ~60–120ms and p95 near target depending on model size and quantization. But exact numbers depend on candidate count and rerank cost.
[05:44] Tom: What about hybrid search — combining BM25 with ANN. How do we ensure we don't miss lexical matches, e.g., drug names or abbreviations?
[05:53] Priya: Yes exact string matches are critical for clinical terms.
[05:57] Diego: Hybrid search helps: use BM25 to capture exact/lexical hits, union with ANN candidates, then dedupe and rerank. We often recommend boosting exact matches before rerank so your reranker retains precision. There are also term-aware tokenization strategies for embeddings.
[06:12] Sarah: any latency overhead for hybrid approach?
[06:15] Diego: Minimal if your BM25 is local and ANN is tuned; the main cost is reranking additional candidates. If you keep candidate set to 50–100, rerank cost dominates.
[06:26] Priya: For ANN library choice, we got good density with HNSW on FAISS, but operationally Milvus had interesting features and Weaviate had DB features we liked. Thoughts?
[06:37] Diego: All common choices. Milvus/Weaviate give managed features; Pinecone simplifies ops but can be more expensive. For on-prem FAISS with HNSW we recommend tuned ef/construction params. We'll share a benchmark template that covers index build time, memory, QPS, and recall curves.
[06:56] Tom: On the pricing side, we'd like to see a Hosted vs Dedicated delta — break down per-token/generation vs per-embedding cost plus reserved capacity for Dedicated.
[07:06] Maya: We'll send a pricing sheet that shows sample monthly cost for your 80 qps baseline and the burst profile. Also include an example Dedicated commitment.
[07:15] Sarah: If we run the benchmark, what do you need from our side?
[07:19] Diego: Ideally a sample corpus (Priya mentioned 20k doc subset), a set of 500 real queries with relevance labels, and any current embedding code. We'll run Dedicated cluster with the candidate sizes you want and measure end-to-end latency and rerank quality.
[07:33] Priya: We can provide that, but we need a little guidance on format.
[07:36] Diego: I'll send the benchmark template with dataset schema and evaluation metrics.
[07:40] Maya: Quick recap and risks: regulatory requirements push you to Dedicated or Private. main unknowns are dimensionality tradeoff and reranker design. we'll run the two-week benchmark to provide concrete latency/cost numbers.
[07:55] Tom: Security checklist items — SSO/SAML support, role-based access, audit logs, and CMK — do you support all?
[08:03] Maya: Yes to all; Private deployment gives you the most control. we'll attach the security packet and include timing for onboarding Private if you choose that route.
[08:13] Sarah: Any gotchas on data egress when using Hosted embeddings + storing vectors in our DB?
[08:18] Diego: There's network egress and potential PHI considerations; for PHI and residency we recommend Dedicated or Private to avoid cross-tenant exposure and to keep everything in your VPC.
[08:29] Priya: One technical nit: KV cache vs prefix cache — how does Redwood manage recurring conversational context?
[08:35] Diego: Our runtime supports KV cache optimizations for autoregressive generation and prefix caching for repeated prompts. For rerank flows it's less relevant but useful for chat-like escalation paths.
[08:46] Sarah: Ok, great. let's lock the next steps.
[08:49] Maya: Next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs by 09-16, Diego will send benchmark template and proposed Dedicated config, you (Priya) will share sample corpus and queries. Then we'll schedule a technical deep dive next week to review the benchmark plan.
[09:05] Tom: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:09] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up over email.

End of transcript.
